# require-is-valid-check

Ensure `@minecraft/server` instances are re-validated with `isValid` before use
after invalidation points (an `await`/`yield`, a deferred callback such as
`system.run`/`system.runTimeout`, or a `for...of` loop whose body awaits).

In the Bedrock Script API, native handles (`Entity`, `Player`, `Block`,
`Container`, …) can become invalid between ticks. Reading most members of an
invalidated handle throws. This rule enforces a defensive `isValid` check (or an
equivalent narrowing) before such references are used.

## How references are classified

- **Plain references** — a tracked type that is _not_ branded as validated
  (e.g. a parameter typed `Player`). These must be validated before any
  non-safe use.
- **Branded references** — a validated reference (e.g. `ValidPlayer`, produced
  by the shipped `valid-types` augmentation). The brand is trusted in the
  synchronous stretch where it was obtained (including sync
  `map`/`filter`/`forEach` callbacks and branded member paths like
  `viewed.block`). An `await`/`yield` that can reach the use clears that trust,
  so a later use must recheck `isValid`. Awaits that only run on a mutually
  exclusive early-exit branch (`if (!x.isValid) { await …; return; }`) do
  **not** taint the continuation. Captures into a deferred callback
  (`system.run`, `runTimeout`, `Promise.then`, an event handler closing over an
  outer handle, …) also require revalidation. Pre-validated event _parameters_
  are valid inside that event callback only; capturing them into a nested
  deferred callback still requires revalidation. Entity-subject after-event
  payloads remain plain (`entitySpawn`, `entityLoad`, `entityDie`,
  `entityHurt`, `entityHitEntity`, `projectileHitEntity`,
  `playerInteractWithEntity.target`, …): after-events dispatch at the end of
  the tick, so the subject entity may already have been removed — e.g. an
  earlier subscriber removes it, or it was killed and despawned by script in
  the same tick. Before-event payloads and acting-player after-event payloads
  (`itemUse.source`, `playerBreakBlock.player`, `chatSend.sender`, …) stay
  branded.
- **Plain aliases** — assigning a plain tracked handle to a new variable does
  **not** make the alias known-valid. Only branded/prevalidated values are
  treated as known-valid at declaration/assignment.

Reads of [`safeProperties`](#options) never require a check, because they do not
throw on invalidated handles. This is **type-scoped**: by default only
`Entity.id` and `Entity.typeId` (inherited by `Player`/`SimulatedPlayer`) are
treated as safe, since those are the only members the API documents as accessible
on an invalid handle. The same `typeId` read on a `Block` or `ContainerSlot`
still requires a check.

Tracked-type matching is **inheritance-aware**: a value is tracked if its type
_or any of its base types_ is listed in `trackedTypes`. This means `Player` is
covered by the `Entity` entry, and every concrete component (e.g.
`EntityInventoryComponent`) is covered by the `Component` entry.

## ✅ Correct

```ts
function onHit(player: Player) {
  if (!player.isValid) return;
  player.kill();
}

// Branded reference obtained and used synchronously.
const player = world.getAllPlayers()[0];
player.kill();
// Fresh onScreenDisplay on a live player is branded — no second isValid.
player.onScreenDisplay.setActionBar('hi');

// Pre-validated event payload used directly.
world.afterEvents.entityHurt.subscribe(event => {
  event.hurtEntity.kill();
});
```

## ❌ Incorrect

```ts
function onHit(player: Player) {
  player.kill(); // player may be invalid
}

const player = world.getAllPlayers()[0];
system.run(() => {
  player.kill(); // branded capture still needs revalidation
});

world.afterEvents.entityHurt.subscribe(event => {
  system.run(() => {
    event.hurtEntity.kill(); // event payload capture needs revalidation
  });
});

function useAlias(player: Player) {
  const alias = player;
  alias.kill(); // plain alias is not known-valid at declaration
}

async function tick() {
  for (const p of world.getAllPlayers()) {
    await system.waitTicks(1);
    p.kill(); // p may be invalid after awaiting
  }
}
```

## Options

```jsonc
{
  "minecraft-isvalid/require-is-valid-check": [
    "error",
    {
      "trackedTypes": ["Entity", "Block", "Component" /* … */],
      "trackedModules": ["@minecraft/server"],
      "safeProperties": { "Entity": ["id", "typeId"] },
    },
  ],
}
```

| Option           | Type                       | Description                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trackedTypes`   | `string[]`                 | Type names (or base types) that must be validated before use.                                 |
| `trackedModules` | `string[]`                 | Modules a tracked type must originate from to be considered.                                  |
| `safeProperties` | `Record<string, string[]>` | Per-type map of members that stay readable regardless of validity (inheritance-aware lookup). |

This rule requires [type information](https://typescript-eslint.io/getting-started/typed-linting).
